page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Left margin holds three note blocks: "Prov. 1." beside the Solomo line, a note of six lines on penitence and charity beside the lines from "Poenite-" to "potest.", and a note of eight lines beside "Genera-" to "re.". Running head at top, page number 120 at top left.

main_text.p: quis non insaniat. Ea nimirū est peccati lues, ut ab aliis ad alios quasi contagione celeriter manet atque diffudatur. Eo spectat quod ait, Prov. 1.Solomo cum esse more peccatoribus, ut alios ad peccandi societate alliciant. Quanto igitur æquius est eum qui virtute colit, alios sanctis monitis in eandem mentem pertrahere, & quasi primus ex coeno surrexerit, sociis manum Poenitē-tia sine fi-de & charita-te esse nō potest.porrigere ut illi etiam emergāt? Adden-dum eodem est, nec poenitentia sine fide, nec rursus fidem sine charitate unquā esse posse. Ex quo efficitur ut cum poenitentia per fidem veras in animis radices egerit, tū charitas erga proximos eorumque salutis cura ac defi-deriū efflorescat. Hoc ergo praestemus neces-se est si Dauidis poenitentia volumus imitari.
Iam propius attendamus ipsa Dauidis verba.

Erudiam te, inquit. Non alienū erit fortase quærere, cur nō in hoc tantū loco, sed in aliis plerisque is sit Scripturæ usus, ut omnibꝰ verba faciens unū sæpissime copellare videa-tur. Genera-les reprehensiones fibi fin-guli de-bent ac-commoda re.Nepe nos vult esse admonitos, siquidē in cohortationibus & reprehensionibus audien-dis proficere volumus, eas esse unicuique no-strū priuatim accommodandas. Ea.n.est natu-rae nostrae prauitas, ut quæ in genere dicūtur, si minus ea grata sunt, respuamus, nec ea nobis dicta esse existimemus. Dānentur vitia in Ecclesiastica cōcione, exagitetur ambitio, avaritia reprehēdatur: tū ambitiōsus aut avarꝰ hęc apud se: Nihil hoc ad me: telū istud aliū serit.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "lues" (printed as "lucs", long s misread), "fi-de" in the penitence note (the middle word "sine" printed as "fine"), "defi-deriū" (the second part of "desiderium" looks abbreviated; kept as printed), "Dānentur" (the abbreviation is uncertain; it may be a damaged form of "Dantur"), "avarꝰ" (a superscript mark after "auar" was read as -us; uncertain), "omnibꝰ" (superscript mark after "omnib" read as -us), "serit" (last word on line before "rit.", the long s was read as s). The margin notes are placed at the lines they stand beside. No catchword, signature or other furniture printed. The page ends mid-sentence with "rit.", which closes the last paragraph.
